channel.title: Bench
channel.description: Updates for Bench, a Mac app for running Claude Code.

item.title: Bench 0.5.6
item.description:
Bench 0.5.6 makes the sidebar sort itself, and lets you send queued messages right away.

  • Active projects take care of themselves. Projects you've worked in lately show under Active, most recent first. Sending Claude a prompt, opening a tab or starting an agent counts, and so does work Claude Code remembers from outside Bench. After a few days without use (3 by default, set in Settings > General) a project moves to Inactive, and it comes back as soon as you use it again.
  • Pin to Top. Right-click a project and choose Pin to Top to keep it at the top of Active. Drag pinned projects to put them in your order. Move to Inactive and Make Active are still there too.
  • The iPhone app matches. With the latest TestFlight build, your phone shows the same Active list and a folding Inactive section, with Pin to Top and Move to Inactive when you long-press a project.
  • Send queued messages now. A message you queued while Claude was busy has a Send Now button, which stops the step Claude is on and hands it your message, like Ctrl+Return in the terminal. Control-Return in the chat view's message box does the same.
  • Compacting no longer stretches the window. Running Compact from the chat view kept the content from fitting the window until it finished. Fixed.

item.title: Bench 0.5.5
item.description:
Bench 0.5.5 adds a few touches to the chat view's message box.

  • Claude's suggested next message. After a turn, Claude Code often guesses what you'll say next and shows it faintly in its terminal. That guess now shows faintly in the chat view's empty message box too. Press Right Arrow or Tab to fill it in, then Return to send. On iPhone it's a chip you can tap.
  • Shift-Return adds a line. Shift-Return (or Option-Return) starts a new line in the message box instead of sending.
  • Context reads with a slash, like "64k / 1M".

item.title: Bench 0.5.4
item.description:
Bench 0.5.4 makes the chat view quicker, smoother, and better at showing what Claude is up to.

  • See Claude's subagents. When Claude sends out agents, each gets a card in the chat with what it's for and what it's doing right now. While they run, they also show in the right sidebar under the checklist, so they don't scroll away. When a background agent or command finishes, a quiet line in the chat says so.
  • Sending feels instant. Your message shows the moment you press Return, and new messages slide in while the conversation glides up to make room.
  • See and change the model. The model Claude is using shows next to the context meter, as soon as a session starts. Click it to switch to Fable, Opus, Sonnet or Haiku.
  • Edit or remove queued messages. A message you sent while Claude was busy now has Edit and Remove under it. The other queued messages stay queued.
  • Compact or clear without typing. The new / menu next to the paperclip runs Compact Conversation or Clear Conversation.
  • Copy a message. Hover over a message and click the copy button beside it.
  • Your draft stays put. Text and pictures in the message box are still there when you switch projects and come back.
  • Picture previews. Pictures you attach or paste show as thumbnails instead of file names.
  • Right-click changed files. Files in the Changes sidebar have a menu to open them, show them in Finder, or copy their full or relative path. The Files tab can copy either path too.
  • Simpler context meter. Context use is now just text, like "64k of 1M", which turns orange and then red as it fills.

item.title: Bench 0.5.3
item.description:
Bench 0.5.3 makes the chat view easier to follow while Claude works.

  • The chat stays at the bottom. New text and tool steps used to pile up out of sight while Claude worked on a long turn. Now the chat follows along as the conversation grows. Scroll up to read something earlier and it stays put, with a button to jump back to the latest. Sending a message always brings you back down.
  • See messages you've queued. A message you send while Claude is busy now shows up right away as a Queued bubble under what Claude is doing. It becomes a normal message once Claude reads it. Before, it didn't appear until then, which could be a whole turn later.
  • Paste images into the chat. Press Command-V in the message box to attach a screenshot, a copied image, or image files copied in Finder. Text still pastes as text.

item.title: Bench 0.5.2
item.description:
Bench 0.5.2 opens long conversations much faster.

  • Big chats open in a moment. Long Claude sessions write transcripts of hundreds of megabytes. The chat view used to read all of it before showing anything, which could take several seconds. Now it reads from the end, just far enough to show the recent conversation, so even the biggest sessions open in well under a second. The top of the chat says when older messages are left out, and nothing in the transcript is changed.
  • Faster on your phone and other Macs too. They get the same speedup when they open a long session on this Mac.

item.title: Bench 0.5.1
item.description:
Bench 0.5.1 brings the chat view's step cards to your phone, and lets the phone dress in your terminal's colors.

  • Your phone in your Mac's colors. The Bench iPhone app (1.1 build 7 and later) can take on the background and text colors of your Ghostty theme, light or dark. You can turn this off from the phone's menu.
  • Edits, commands and Stop on the phone. The phone now shows the lines Claude changed, whether each command worked and what it printed, and a Stop button while Claude is working. This needs the new phone build too.
  • Other Macs get the same. When you watch a Claude session on another Mac, you see command results and can stop Claude from there.
  • Stopped commands say so. A command you stopped or denied now reads "Stopped" instead of "Failed".

item.title: Bench 0.5
item.description:
Bench 0.5 lets you read and run any Claude tab as a chat, right on your Mac.

  • Chat or terminal, per tab. Switch a Claude tab between its terminal and a chat with the buttons in the tab bar, or View > Show as Chat (⌥⌘T). Claude keeps running in the terminal either way, so the raw terminal is always one click away. Settings > General picks which one new Claude tabs start in.
  • In your terminal's colors. The chat uses your Ghostty theme, light or dark, so it looks like part of Bench rather than a separate app.
  • See what Claude did. Files it read sit on a quiet timeline, and you can click one to open it. Edits show the lines that changed. Commands show whether they worked and the last lines they printed.
  • Where you're reading. The end of the conversation shows what Claude is doing or that it's waiting on you, with a timer and a Stop button.
  • Answer with the keyboard. When Claude asks to run something, Return allows it and Escape denies it, just like in the terminal. Questions and permissions get cards right above the message box.

item.title: Bench 0.4.2
item.description:
Bench 0.4.2 makes answering Claude from your phone or another Mac smoother.

  • Trust a new folder from anywhere. When Claude starts in a folder it hasn't opened before, it asks whether you trust it before doing anything else. That question used to show up only in the Mac's terminal, so a session started from your phone got stuck. Now it appears as a card you can answer from your phone or another Mac. Bench only passes your answer along. It never trusts a folder for you.
  • Answers take effect right away. After you allow or deny a permission from another device, the card goes away as soon as Bench has your answer. Before, it stayed until Claude moved on, which made it look like the tap hadn't worked. Answered questions clear the same way, and the tab stops showing orange on the Mac.

Trusting a folder from your phone needs the latest Bench beta for iPhone.

item.title: Bench 0.4.1
item.description:
Bench 0.4.1 fixes two problems some people saw after updating to 0.4.

  • Your Active projects stay Active. Restarting Bench soon after opening it could move every project to Inactive. Bench now keeps your Active list no matter when you quit or update.
  • ⌘1 to ⌘9 always work. If your Active list was empty when Bench opened, the shortcuts for jumping between Active projects didn't come back after you marked projects Active again. They now follow the list as it changes.

If your projects moved to Inactive after the 0.4 update, mark them Active once more and they'll stay that way.

item.title: Bench 0.4
item.description:
Bench 0.4 tells you what's new, answers Claude's questions from anywhere, and gives the terminal a softer edge.

See what's new. When an update is ready, the button at the bottom of the sidebar shows what's in it before you restart. After Bench updates, a What's New window lists everything that changed since the version you last used. You can open it any time from Bench > What's New in Bench.

Answer Claude's questions from another Mac. When Claude asks you a multiple-choice question, you can now answer it while watching the session from another Mac: pick an option, tick several where it allows, or write your own answer. Bench enters it on the Mac where Claude is running. The tab also turns orange as soon as Claude asks, instead of a few seconds later.

Compacting is easy to spot. While Claude compacts a conversation you're watching from another Mac, a banner says so, and the conversation shows a clear "Conversation compacted" card afterward instead of a line of small gray text.

Answering questions and the compacting banner come to the iPhone app in its next update.

A rounded terminal. The terminal, diffs, and files now sit in the window as a card with rounded corners, below a tab bar that matches the sidebars.

Claude tabs that are already open pick up question and compacting detection the next time Claude starts in them.

item.title: Bench 0.3.1
item.description:
Bench 0.3.1 makes the window match your terminal.

Matches your terminal theme. The sidebar, toolbar, changes panel, diffs, and files now use the colors of your Ghostty theme, and the window goes light or dark to match it. If your theme switches between light and dark with the system, Bench follows along. Prefer the system look? Turn off "Match the terminal theme" in Settings > General.

Also:

  • The button that shows and hides the changes panel is back on the right side of the toolbar, above the panel it opens.
  • The app icon's chevron no longer shows a thin line through it.

item.title: Bench 0.3
item.description:
Bench 0.3 gets Bench ready for other people to use, and adds a few things you'll notice right away.

Your own tab shortcuts. Add one-click tabs for commands you run often in Settings > Shortcuts. They show up at the right of the tab bar and in the + menu, and can be limited to one project or to projects with a certain file. JavaScript projects also get a dev server button that runs dev with the project's package manager.

Setup checklist. Bench now checks for Claude Code, git, the GitHub CLI, and Tailscale, and shows what it found with links to anything missing. It appears once on first launch and lives in Settings > Setup. Bench also finds these tools the same way your shell does, so tools installed outside Homebrew work too.

Safer agent cleanup. When an agent's pull request merges, Bench only removes its worktree if nothing would be lost: no uncommitted or unpushed work. Removed worktrees go to the Trash. Automatic cleanup is now a setting in Settings > General, and it's off by default.

Updates ask first. New installs ask before checking for updates. Installing an update while the Mac is idle is now a setting in Settings > Updates, off by default.

iPhone companion.

  • Bench no longer replaces an existing Tailscale Serve setup. If something else is using it, Bench uses a /bench path instead.
  • The phone can only read files that show up in the project's file list.

Also:

  • Bench > Acknowledgements credits Ghostty, Sparkle, and the other open source projects Bench is built on.
  • Bench saves less of what Claude passes to its tools. Whole file contents no longer sit in Bench's support folder.

item.title: Bench 0.2
item.description:
This is the first version of Bench that keeps itself up to date.

  • Automatic updates. New versions download in the background. They install when you quit Bench or click Restart to Update at the bottom of the sidebar. If Claude is busy, Bench asks before restarting, and Claude tabs pick up their conversations afterward. A Mac nobody is using installs updates by itself after 30 minutes with nothing running.
  • Files sidebar. The right sidebar has a Changes / Files switch. Files shows the project's folders and updates as files come and go. Click a file to open it in a tab with line numbers that reloads as Claude edits it. This works for projects on your other Macs too.
  • Your messages in remote conversations. Messages you send while Claude is busy, and messages that start with a paste, now show up when you watch a session from another Mac or your iPhone.

Settings has a new Updates tab with the version and a switch for automatic checks.
